facts.fact: Law 12/2018 of 4 December 2018 creates SIRCEV and rests it on the National Directorate of Registries and Notaries, with the provincial justice directorates coordinating and the civil registry conservatórias executing and administering registration operations, nationwide.

Law 12/2018 provides that the birth and death books of the conservatórias are replaced by electronic entries, with other books replaced gradually and the paper kept as proof where it contradicts the electronic record; this is what the law provides, not a count of what offices do.

Law 12/2018 (revised article 18) makes each conservatória responsible for carrying out the electronic registration itself and then remitting it to the central registry services, and lets a certificate of an electronically made record be requested at any conservatória in the country; this is what the law provides, not a count of what offices do.

The Civil Registration Code as captured with Law 12/2018 (article 13) creates a centralised database at the Central Registries Conservatória in which all civil registration acts are recorded by transcription, every registry office sending full-copy certificates of the previous month's acts by the tenth of each month.
